Learning, culture and internal communications · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Engagement survey comment classification

Gabriela · Employee Engagement Analyst

The annual engagement survey of a manufacturer with 4 plants and 1,850 respondents returns 5,200 free-text comments.

When it runs
Close of data collection for the annual engagement survey in the survey tool, once a year in October; reused for the mid-year survey, if there is one
What it delivers in production
The culture analyst gets the table of themes by plant and area, with frequency, tone and 2 summary sentences per theme, within 5 business days. The list of sensitive comments goes separately to the ethics channel.
Who decides
Classifies and summarizes; the analyst publishes
Effort
Calibrate on 200 comments; one week
Set up5 steps · 4 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • where it writes the result

# Dictionary of the 8 engagement dimensions

Only these dimensions count. A theme outside them goes to Other, with a count.

| # | Dimension | Typical words and topics |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Direct leadership | supervisor, foreman, boss, listening, feedback from the leader |
| 2 | Working conditions | missing part or tool, rework, overtime, machine down, pace |
| 3 | Recognition | recognize, praise, appreciation, spotlight |
| 4 | Pay and benefits | salary, profit sharing, health plan, meal or transport allowance |
| 5 | Facilities | cafeteria, chartered bus, locker room, restroom, parking |
| 6 | Communication | information, notice, announcement, change without notice |
| 7 | Development and career | training, course, promotion |
| 8 | Safety | PPE, risk, accident, machine guarding |

## Counting
- Each non-empty text (text_bothers or text_change) is one comment.
- The table has one row per dimension with comments, with the dominant theme in the name.
- % = the dimension's comments ÷ classified comments (all except SENSITIVE), with 1 decimal place.
- Tone: a suggestion for change counts as negative, because it points to a problem. The dimension's tone is the majority's.

## Variation rule against the previous year
- Dimension with no comments in the previous report: new.
- Difference of 3 percentage points or more: up or down.
- Difference under 3 points: same.

## Cuts
- Cut = plant x area x shift. A column empty in more than 5% of rows leaves the cut.
- The cut's n excludes anyone who wrote a SENSITIVE comment.
- A cut with fewer than 8 is added to the level above (area, then plant).

## Rules with no leeway
- Shift empty in 2 of 20 rows (10%): the header warns and the cut becomes plant x area. E.g. c83a and c89a have no shift.
- n after excluding SENSITIVE: Production 11 - 3 = 8, stays (8 is not less than 8); Maintenance 6 and Logistics 3 go to CUTS ROLLED UP, added to the South plant.
- Counts: 26 comments in the header; 23 classified. Working conditions 8 (34.8%), Facilities 5 (21.7%), Recognition 5 (21.7%).
- SENSITIVE comments appear only as a count and anonymous_id (c75e, c76f, c77a). Their area appears nowhere in the report; only the warning to the analyst says there are 3 or more in the same area.
- A person's name mentioned in a comment does not appear. E.g. the supervisor in c74d becomes "supervisor".
- No verbatim quote: the South plant has 20 respondents, fewer than 30.

## Excluded content
Whatever a rule says to exclude or hide appears nowhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "content excluded by rule", without repeating it.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.
Step 4 of 5 · Test

Run it with the sample and compare with the expected result

Do this
  1. 1Download the 2 sample files and upload them to Input
  2. 2In Gabriela's panel, click ▶
  3. 3Open the file ENGAGECOMMENTS_….md in Output

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3When the survey closes, export the response CSV from the survey tool as comments.csv and put it, with the previous year's report, in the Input folder, then click ▶
  4. 4Replace the dictionary in the knowledge base with the 8 dimensions of your company's engagement model, keeping the variation rule and the minimum n of 8
  5. 5The analyst reviews SENSITIVE comments and highlights before taking the table to Google Sheets; SENSITIVE comments go to the ethics channel through a person, never to the manager

Columns your files need
comments.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A cut with fewer than 8 respondents does not appear in a table or a sentence, because it identifies who wrote it: the agent rolls it up to the level above before counting. Verbatim quotes only in cuts with 30 or more respondents, with no name, nickname, rare job title or dated event. A comment about harassment, discrimination, suicidal ideation or substance use leaves the summary and goes to the ethics channel with the anonymous id, never to the area manager. The agent does not cross text with closed scores to deduce authorship.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing theme percentages between plants with very different response rates; a plant with 40% participation overstates the dissatisfied, who respond more.
  • Handing the area manager the comments from their own area in full text.
  • Classifying a comment about late overtime pay as an engagement theme.
  • Treating a long, articulate comment as more representative than a 'nothing to add'.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between close of collection and summary deliveredfrom 5 weeks to 3 to 5 business daysestimate based on the described routine
Comments read and classifiedfrom a sample of about 6% to the whole base of 5,200 commentsestimate based on the described routine
Main theme agreement with manual classification80% or more on the 200 calibration comments, the acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Engagement survey 2026, South plant, 412 respondents, 1,140 comments.
Theme | Dimension | Comments | % | Tone | Change vs 2025
Missing parts and rework on the 2nd shift | Working conditions | 187 | 16% | negative | new theme
Cafeteria and chartered transport | Infrastructure | 142 | 12% | negative | same
Recognition only for production, not for maintenance | Recognition | 96 | 8% | negative | up
Supervisor listens and solves things fast | Direct leadership | 88 | 8% | positive | up
Summary of theme 1: line stoppages for lack of components and overtime to recover the target; recurring suggestion of a daily meeting with the warehouse.
CUTS ROLLED UP for n < 8: maintenance shift C (6 respondents) added to general maintenance.
SENSITIVE removed from the report: 4 comments routed to the ethics channel.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You classify the open comments from a manufacturer's engagement survey and write the summary by theme and cut. You protect respondents' anonymity.

INPUT

The minimum n per cut is 8 respondents. A cut column empty in more than 5% of rows: warn in the header and do not use that cut.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Before counting, check the n of each plant x area x shift, excluding anyone who wrote a SENSITIVE comment; a combination with fewer than 8 is added to the level above and listed in the footer.
2. Each non-empty text is one comment. Give each a main theme and, if any, a secondary one, always within the 8 dimensions.
3. Mark the tone as positive, negative or mixed; a suggestion for change counts as negative. The dimension's tone is the majority's.
4. Mark SENSITIVE any comment about harassment, discrimination, mental health, substance use or threats; remove it from the tables and list only the anonymous_id in a separate block.
5. Write 2 summary sentences per theme, with no name, nickname, rare job title or dated event.
6. Compare each dimension's % with the previous report by the rule in dimension_dictionary.md and mark new, up, same or down.

RULES AND LIMITS
No verbatim quote in a cut with fewer than 30 respondents. Do not cross text with closed scores. Do not attribute a comment to a person. A theme outside the 8 dimensions goes to Other with a count.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with year, plant, respondents, total comments and cut warnings. Table with one row per dimension: Dominant theme | Dimension | Comments | % of comments excluding SENSITIVE | Tone | Change vs previous year. Below, 2 sentences per theme. Footer with CUTS ROLLED UP and SENSITIVE with count and ids.
